**Checkpointing trades recomputation for fewer stored activations.** Ordinary backpropagation keeps intermediate values from the forward pass so gradients can use them later. Instead, save selected boundaries and recompute missing values when backward reaches each segment. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1604.06174)

For L equal layers split into segments of length s, save roughly L/s boundaries and at most s internal activations while recomputing one segment. The idealized activation count is proportional to L/s+s. Differentiating the continuous approximation gives $-L/s^2+1=0$, so s is about the square root of L.

With L=100, segments of ten suggest about ten boundaries plus ten active internal values rather than storing all hundred, ignoring constants and endpoint details. The price is executing some forward computations again.

**This is not a square-root bound on all GPU memory.** Parameters, gradients, optimizer states, and temporary attention buffers remain. Unequal layer sizes and branching graphs change the best schedule. Preserve randomness and mutable state during replay so recomputation matches the intended forward computation. Measure actual peak memory and step time; the formula explains one simple schedule under explicit assumptions.

**Technical details and references.**

For a simple chain of $L$ equal-cost/equal-memory layers, divide it into segments of length $s$. Store about $L/s$ boundaries and at most $s$ recomputed internal activations at a time. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1604.06174)

$$M(s)=O(L/s+s),\qquad s\approx\sqrt L\Rightarrow M=O(\sqrt L).$$

This concerns activations under an idealized checkpoint schedule, not total model memory. Parameters, optimizer states, non-chain graphs, attention buffers, unequal layers, and recomputation strategy change practical behavior. Other schedules achieve different memory/compute tradeoffs. Preserve randomness and state semantics during replay and measure peak allocated/reserved device memory rather than claiming every checkpointed network has exactly square-root total memory.
